messages.content:
You are an experienced UK building control surveyor. Answer the question about the work item
in the JSON state. Choose exactly one label:
- not_notifiable: No Building Regulations notice needed: not building work (reg 3), only Schedule 4 work, or an exempt building (reg 9, Schedule 2).
- competent_person_scheme: Notifiable work listed in Schedule 3: a registered competent person can self-certify it (reg 12(6)(a)); otherwise a building notice is needed.
- building_notice_or_full_plans: Building work not covered by Schedules 3 or 4: a building notice or a full plans application to building control (reg 12(2)).
- full_plans_required: Building work that must have a full plans application: the Fire Safety Order applies to the building (reg 12(3)), it fronts a private street (12(4)), or H4 applies (building over or near a sewer, 12(5)).
Reply with JSON only: {"label": "<one label>", "probabilities": {"<label>": <0..1>, ...}} with a
probability for every label, summing to 1.

Under the Building Regulations 2010 in England, which notification route applies to this work item if it is carried out on its own in the building described?

{"work_item": "Wet-room tanking", "project": "Renovation of a terraced house (dwelling) in England. Trade: Wet rooms. Part of: whole-house renovation including loft conversion and rear extension.", "jurisdiction": "England. The Building Regulations 2010 as amended.", "clauses": [{"ref": "para 11.3", "document": "ADL1-2021", "text": "11.3 If a thermal element is renovated and one of the following applies, then the whole of the thermal element should be improved to achieve at least the U-value given in Table 4.3, column (b). a. More than 50% of the surface of the individual thermal element is renovated (see paragraph 11.4). b. The work constitutes a major renovation. A major renovation is when more than 25% of the surface area of the external building envelope is renovated. NOTE: If paragraph 4.13 applies, Appendix C provides examples of renovation of an existing thermal element that are technically, functionally or economically feasible."}, {"ref": "para 11.6", "document": "ADL1-2021", "text": "11.6 A change to energy status is when a dwelling was previously exempt from the energy efficiency requirements but now is not. The change to energy status applies to the building as a whole or to parts of the building that have been designed or altered to be used separately. For example, when a previously unheated space becomes part of the heated dwelling in a garage or loft conversion, a change to energy status applies to that space. NOTE: A material change of use may result in a change to energy status, for example if a previously unheated loft is converted into a flat."}, {"ref": "para 3.25", "document": "ADF1-2021", "text": "3.25 When a wet room is added to an existing dwelling, whole dwelling ventilation should be extended and extract ventilation should be provided by one of the following means. a. Intermittent extract, as specified in Table 1.1, and a background ventilator of at least 5000mm2 equivalent area. b. Continuous extract, as specified in Table 1.2. c. Single-room heat recovery ventilator, as detailed in paragraph 3.26."}]}

message.content:
Wet-room tanking on its own is most likely **not notifiable**. Applying a waterproof membrane to walls and floors is not "building work" under reg 3. It is not an extension or a material alteration, and it does not add a controlled service or fitting.

The quoted ADF 3.25 duty to extend ventilation applies when a wet room is *added* to a dwelling. That would bring in extract fans,
message.reasoning: Applying tanking membrane to an existing bathroom on its own isn't building work under reg 3 unless it's part of creating a new wet room with associated ventilation and drainage changes, and it doesn't affect the structure enough to count as a material alteration.
